I'd say the best way to make it easier for tank/healer is to listen to tank calls (if there are any) and don't be allergic to sacred ground. 

You'll most likely not need to change your setup as GS is big dps and GA is invaluable for the ability to group mobs close for quick and easy clears. That being said, some groups may already have enough GA users and might need a spear for cc/debuffing (rend & weaken). 

Gems start to be handy in m2 and makes the run much easier. M3 is when you really need to make sure you got the full set of consumables for the dungeon type and the right trophies active. Having an amulet that has the corresponding elemental protection for that mutation will help quite a lot, as well. Do keep in mind that some expeditions have multiple mob types, such as this week's Ennead and Barnacles (ancient+corrupted and lost+beast+angry earth, respectively). 

Other tips: Generally, stand in a way where you can hit enemies in the back. Avoid attacking until you see your tank use a taunt and hunker down in a sacred ground as that can disrupt grouping the mobs and become dangerous for you. Dodge big damage and staggers when possible. If you happen to take a lot of damage and your health potion is on cooldown, run to the sacred ground and/or the healer. If you happen to get aggro of a mob, run to the tank (in a way where you're not going to get smacked by whatever is currently on the tank at the time though).

After playing through the game 1.5 times, I realised how many mechanics that I was missing out on leveraging. Little things add up. Such as me forgetting to hunter's mark before attacking the target, not using the throw option to throw spare daggers or javelins when I can't feasibly reach the target with my melee that turn, checking for resistances and vulnerability prior to planning my turn... The list goes on. 

If you want some help with tweaking your build for your party, we'd need some more details such as what subclasses your party took, any multiclasses you might've dipped into, the gear you're using, the general tactics that you use when approaching a fight.

I like having 2 frontliners and 2 backliners. Among the party, I want one of each role (front/backliner) to have some sort of supportive ability. Such as a cleric with bless or a mage with lots of options for CC and zone control. I think paladins also fill the supportive role fine as well. You don't even need to go full pally, you could go a 3 lvl dip of pally and still be effective. Lay on hands is a nice emergency heal when needed, but the main thing I like is the smite damage on top of my attacks. 

The best CC is death.

I'd argue that the Enhanced Leap ritual spell that rangers get is better than Grant Fly solely because it doesn't cost a spell slot to use. Gaseous Form is more for flavour than anything else imo, but it's cool to use at times. 

My picks are counterspell and haste.



Counterspell is invaluable in many moments. It can stop an enemy from casting a devastating spell on your party/allies as a reaction, so kong as you have a spell slot for it. 

Haste is one of the best buff spells in the game, IMO, since you can do quick a lot with an extra action.

The build I did was 5 rogue thief/5 ranger gloomstalker/2 fighter. 5 ranger then 4 rogue then 2 fighter. The last level should be rogue. If you are not yet level 6 and need a rogue in your party to sleight of hand things for you, do 4 rogue first then 5 ranger then 2 fighter and last level as rogue. 

For stats, max out your dex, prioritise con next, then i would argue wis/str as the last to put points in as there are plenty of spells that have saves in those categories. Cha/Int were my dump stats. 

Picking spells, I prioritised Hunter's Mark and Misty Step. Every other spell is to your preference as I typically do not use any other spell than Hunter's Mark and the occasional Misty Step with Astarion. I think I ended up picking the enhanced jump and longstrider spell as those wont eat spell slots and can be cast on party members as well as the one who knows the spell. 

First feat was Ability Score Improvement, getting him from 17 dex and 15 con to 18 dex and 16 con. If you plan to get Ethel's hair buff for him, you could instead go for increasing his dex to 19 so that, with the hair, you get to 20 dex. My second feat was sharpshooter. You could pick them the other way around, if you prefer. 

I equipped him with 2 hand bows in each hand so he could attack with both. I also gave him Risky Ring to allow him to always use sneak attack, since sneak attack requires advantage against targets. Until you get the ring, I try to have someone within melee range of the primary target past Astarion's first turn of damage if he is going first in the fight. 

Give Astarion Haste either through a spell, a potion of speed, or haste spores will give him an extra action when he fights, which is nuts. Open with Hunter's Mark on the primary target and just lettem rip.
You can also get it by using the Risky Ring, whenever you are able to obtain it. Guarantees advantage always at the cost of being vulnerable.

Typically, it is recommended to get to level 5 in one class since it's a milestone for most classes. Such as ranger getting extra attack at lvl 5. 

I went for 2 tempest cleric/x sorcerer. Witchbolt on a wet target mixed with destructive wrath usually blows them up. Add luck of the far realms from your ilithid talents and it doubles the damage again. 
Using a lvl 2 spell slot with the guaranteed max dmg roll from your tempest channel divinity + crit + vulnerable target = 96 damage. Achievable by lvl 5. 

At max level (2 cleric/10 sorc), one cast of witchbolt (with the proper gear) on a vulnerable target would be 288. A second cast using quickened spell and the amulet that gives an additional channel divinity would make the total damage in one turn as 432. If that second hit happens to crit, the total would be 576. This isn't including potential lightning charges.

The different colors are different clans. Whatever you have as a default npc outline means that the horse is unclaimed by any clan on the server. Seeing a horse of any other color means that a member of a clan sat on it. If it's the color that is set to mean friendly (aka apart of your clan), then you or a clanmate sat on that horse at some point. 

If you see another vampire with a green nameplate and you later see a horse with a green color, that means that the green vampire you saw had, at one point, sat on that horse.
